producer_report.summary: The ontology test now checks term content against its governing sources, not only the file's structure. The root cause was that a multi-sense term, Hermes as the studied agent and as the Orchestration god, could be defined from one source and still pass. Jobs 20261017-173508-0wtc and 20261025-214509-y179 both passed checks of structure or activity while the content was wrong or unmeasured. The change adds a check in crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs. For each term, every line in BRIEF.md and in the term's own file sources that names it (whole word or phrase, ignoring case) must match a marker of a listed `senses` entry, or an `excused` entry with a reason. A sense's label must appear in the definition. docs/ontology.toml has the new optional fields, with Hermes tracked by sense markers. The other terms use per-source excuses with recorded reasons. In-memory tests cover the Hermes case: the tool listed alone is flagged, both senses listed passes, and an excuse without a reason fails. D152 and a CHANGELOG entry record the change. The speed-work files, athena.toml, defaults.toml and the workflows are untouched.

open_issues: Blanket per-source excuses for job, Athena, planning and similar terms do not catch a new second sense in those sources. D152 records this tradeoff.
y179's speed work (measure-first stage) is out of scope and untouched.
mistakes: The first draft of the check was run against the real file with no senses or excuses, which produced hundreds of failures. I then added the per-source excuses.
learnings: BRIEF.md names common terms (job, Athena, planning) hundreds of times, so line-level accounting needs source-level excuses with reasons for them. Only Hermes, whose hits are few and distinctive, is tracked by per-sense markers.
The decision log guard accepts a new Dnnn entry with the standard fields appended at the end.
desires: A way to list term hits per file, since grep was not allowed through Bash.
